Implementation Plan

Implementation plan: issue #6224, keep the unblock judge's bulk-delete override away from workflow and automation paths in every repository

Planning ref: `git rev-parse HEAD` = `454c65dc3b59a1b704a8e5faa49f0e8eb6eff3b6`, branch `claude/replace-claude-sessions-phase-7`. That matches the issue's integration branch metadata (no mismatch).

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends CANONICAL_SOURCE_RE
Scope-mode justification: The finding is real. In `scripts/unblock_ledger.py::validate()` (lines 416-419), the `FORBIDDEN_OVERRIDE_PREFIXES` check (`.github/workflows/`, `.claude/`, `scripts/`) runs only when `repo == SOURCE_REPO`. The destructive branch (lines 420-424) checks only `CANONICAL_SOURCE_RE`, and that pattern does not cover `.github/workflows/` or `.claude/`. Both deletion guards apply the override whenever `canonical_deletions` is empty: `scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh` around lines 453-460, and the "Preflight destructive-commit guard" in `.github/workflows/implement.yml` around lines 3489-3496. That grep uses the same canonical pattern. In a consumer repo with `ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS=true` (the default), an `override=bulk_delete` marker that lists `.github/workflows/*.yml` therefore lifts `BULK_DELETE_THRESHOLD` for those deletions. The fix stays inside the issue's scope. It adds one shared denylist of protected automation paths next to the existing canonical list, applies it to the destructive override in every repository, and enforces it in both deletion guards. Enforcing it in the guards also blocks markers posted before the fix. The complete version costs well under 30 extra lines over the shortcut and adds no dependency or interface, so per §6 (Security > Correctness & safety > …) the guard-side enforcement is included, not just the validator change. Scope-blocked overrides in consumer repos are deliberately left unchanged (see Risks).

1. Files likely to change
- `scripts/unblock_ledger.py`: new denylist constant, destructive-branch check in `validate()`, and the module docstring's rule text (lines 30-34).
- `scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh`: the destructive-commit guard (block starting line 396) and its header comment.
- `.github/workflows/implement.yml`: the "Preflight destructive-commit guard" step (block around lines 3440-3500). The file is 317,823 bytes; this adds about 8 lines, far below the 480,000-byte guard (§24).
- `prompts/mode-judge-unblock.txt` and `prompts/_templates/mode-judge-unblock.txt`: the hard-rules line (line 27 and line 20 respectively). The two files must stay identical apart from the include line.
- `tests/test_unblock_judge.py`: new validator cases.
- `tests/test_unblock_scan.py`: extend `test_bulk_override_never_covers_canonical_deletions`.
- `tests/test_implement_post_codex_recovery.py`: one behavioural preflight test.
- `agents.md`: the "Unblock judge (Phase 7)" bullet's sentence on bulk-delete verdict comments and `Approved deletions`.
- `changelog.d/6224-unblock-override-protected-paths.md`: new fragment, following the format and voice rules in CLAUDE.md §20.

2. Functions or modules to implement
- `scripts/unblock_ledger.py`
  - Add, next to `CANONICAL_SOURCE_RE` (line 124):
    `PROTECTED_AUTOMATION_OVERRIDE_RE = re.compile(r"^(\.github|\.claude|workflow-templates)(/|$)", re.IGNORECASE)`
    Comment that both deletion guards keep an identical grep in step with it, the same way the existing comment ties `CANONICAL_SOURCE_RE` to the guard grep. Before adding the name, grep the repo to confirm it is unique (§10).
  - In `validate()`, in the `decision.get("stop") == "destructive-blocked"` branch, keep the `CANONICAL_SOURCE_RE` check exactly as it is. Add a second check that raises `UsageError(f"override_guard never allows bulk-deleting the protected automation path {path!r}")` when `PROTECTED_AUTOMATION_OVERRIDE_RE.match(path)`. This runs in every repository: no `repo` condition.
  - Leave the source-repo `FORBIDDEN_OVERRIDE_PREFIXES` check unchanged; it still governs scope-blocked overrides in this repo.
  - Update the docstring rule: for the destructive latch, no path may be a canonical workflow source, or under `.github/`, `.claude/` or `workflow-templates/`, in any repository.
- Both deletion guards (`scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh` and the implement.yml preflight step):
  - Right after `canonical_deletions=…`, add:
    `unblock_protected_deletions="$(printf '%s\n' "${deleted_staged}" | grep -iE '^(\.github|\.claude|workflow-templates)/' || true)"`
    Grep first to confirm `unblock_protected_deletions` is not already used in either file.
  - Extend the override condition while keeping the existing line verbatim, because the current contract test asserts its exact substring:
    ```
    if [ "${UNBLOCK_BULK_DELETE_OVERRIDE:-false}" = "true" ] && [ -z "${canonical_deletions}" ] &&
      [ -z "${unblock_protected_deletions}" ] &&
      printf ... jq ... ; then
    ```
  - When the override is set but `unblock_protected_deletions` is non-empty, print one log line:
    `UNBLOCK_BULK_DELETE_OVERRIDE outcome=skip reason=protected_automation_paths`
    This reuses the existing `UNBLOCK_BULK_DELETE_OVERRIDE` stable prefix; no new prefix is added. Normal threshold handling then runs unchanged (`destructive_commit_blocked=bulk-delete` when over the threshold).
  - Update the comment above the override ("never when a canonical workflow source…") to name the protected automation paths too, and note the matching header-comment change in `implement_commit_changes.sh`.
- Prompts: change the hard rule to two bullets:
  - "`override_guard` never covers `.github/workflows/`, `.claude/` or `scripts/` in shubhodeep1/coding-workflows." (unchanged)
  - "For the destructive guard, `override_guard` never lists a canonical workflow source (`agents.md`, `ai_pipeline.md`, `unattended_system_instructions.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `prompts/`, `scripts/`, `.github/ai/`, `.github/scripts/`) or any path under `.github/`, `.claude/` or `workflow-templates/`, in any repository."

3. Data structures affected
- None persisted. The marker format `<!-- ai:unblock:v1 … override=bulk_delete -->`, the `Approved deletions: [...]` line, the step outputs (`destructive_commit_blocked`, `destructive_commit_count`, …) and env vars (`UNBLOCK_BULK_DELETE_OVERRIDE`, `UNBLOCK_BULK_DELETE_PATHS`) are all unchanged.

4. API or interface changes
- No CLI, env-var or JSON-field changes.
- Behaviour changes:
  - `unblock_ledger.py validate` now exits 1 for a destructive `override_guard` that lists a protected automation path, in any repository. `unblock_judge.sh` already treats a refused verdict as invalid (line 531).
  - The guards no longer apply the override when protected automation paths are among the staged deletions.

## Decisions

### D1 — Enforce in both the validator and both deletion guards
- Chosen: reject in `unblock_ledger.py::validate()` and also exclude protected deletions from the override in `implement_commit_changes.sh` and the implement.yml preflight.
- Alternatives considered: validator only (as the finding names it); guards only.
- Why: with the validator alone, override markers already posted on consumer issues would stay usable. With the guards alone, the judge would keep posting overrides that can never apply. The recommendation asks for both, and repeating the check is the repo's existing pattern (`CANONICAL_SOURCE_RE` already mirrors the guard grep).

### D2 — Denylist covers the whole `.github/` tree, `.claude/` and `workflow-templates/`, case-insensitive
- Chosen: `^(\.github|\.claude|workflow-templates)(/|$)` with IGNORECASE, added alongside `CANONICAL_SOURCE_RE`, which is not changed.
- Alternatives considered: `.github/workflows/` only; reusing `FORBIDDEN_OVERRIDE_PREFIXES` for every repository; changing `CANONICAL_SOURCE_RE` itself.
- Why: `.github/actions/`, CODEOWNERS and dependabot config are also automation. `FORBIDDEN_OVERRIDE_PREFIXES` includes `scripts/`, which `CANONICAL_SOURCE_RE` already covers. Widening `CANONICAL_SOURCE_RE` would also change the guard's `canonical-source` rejection, so `ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS=false` would start hard-failing ordinary workflow deletions. That is a behaviour change outside scope (§9). Case-insensitivity can only make the override stricter.

### D3 — Leave scope-blocked overrides unchanged
- Chosen: the new check applies only to `stop == "destructive-blocked"`.
- Alternatives considered: apply the denylist to scope-blocked overrides in every repository too.
- Why: the finding and recommendation are about destructive overrides. Consumer tasks that legitimately edit their own workflows depend on scope overrides, and the existing test `test_override_never_covers_protected_paths_in_coding_workflows` deliberately asserts that consumers are allowed.

## Security considerations
- Trust boundaries touched:
  - Model output (the unblock judge verdict JSON, untrusted) into `validate()`.
  - Issue comments into the implement.yml override-spend step. The marker is trusted only from the pipeline login, and its `Approved deletions` list is only as safe as the validator that produced it.
  - The staged git deletion set into the commit guards.
- Authorization: no new endpoint or surface. The override is still spendable once and only from a trusted-login marker. Existing `ALLOW_BULK_DELETE` and `ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS` operator controls are unchanged.
- Input validation: `_clean_path` already rejects globs, `..`, absolute paths and non-ASCII characters. The new check runs on the cleaned paths. The guard side uses exact-path `jq index` plus the new protected-path grep.
- Abuse cases closed:
  - A prompt-injected issue or evidence leads the judge to emit `override_guard` with `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` plus several others on a consumer repo, so the implementer can mass-delete CI or security workflows past the threshold. Now refused by the validator, and the guard ignores the override.
